subject: Quantapay availability gap — compensation approach & RCA meeting
messages:
From: Alyssa Murray <alyssa.murray@quantapay.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@quantapay.com
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: 2029-03-28 availability gap — confirmation & compensation

Hi Vanessa / David,

We saw a sustained failure mode against your hosted inference endpoints on 2029-03-28 between ~03:40-04:15 UTC that resulted in ~8% of our checkout requests returning 503s. This materially impacted our peak morning hours and resulted in a manual rollback and throttling on our side.

Can you confirm the exact window you observed for service unavailability? We need a concise statement of impact (start/end, regions) and your proposed compensation approach under our SLA so we can present to the ops and finance teams.

Attached is a short sample of our client-side errors (quantapay-sample-errors.log). Please also include a proposed time for a quick RCA session — we'd prefer tomorrow morning PT if possible.

Thanks,

Alyssa Murray
Head of Site Reliability, QuantaPay
alyssa.murray@quantapay.com
(415) 555-0199

-----

On Wed, 10 Apr 2029 at 11:03 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
To: Alyssa Murray <alyssa.murray@quantapay.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: 2029-03-28 availability gap — confirmation & compensation

Thanks for the heads up, Alyssa — sorry for the trouble this caused your team. We're pulling the timeline and a telemetry bundle now.

Quick answers up front:
- We see a regional routing anomaly in US-WEST-2 tied to an autoscaler misconfiguration that produced elevated 503s for a subset of pooled hosts.
- Preliminary window: 2029-03-28 03:38:12 UTC -> 2029-03-28 04:17:09 UTC. We're still validating the tail behavior.

Can we schedule a 30-minute RCA tomorrow (Thu Apr 11) 09:00 AM PT? I'll include the initial trace bundle and a draft compensation calculation for your review.

Attachments referenced below once the bundle finishes uploading.

Regards,

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

-----

Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: 2029-03-28 availability gap — confirmation & compensation

Looping in the commercial perspective: Karthik — FYI on the Quantapay impact.

Alyssa — from precedent we typically offer a prorated credit calculated over the impacted minutes relative to monthly committed usage, with an additional one-time operational credit when the incident crosses customer-impact thresholds (like sustained 5%+ errors for >20 minutes during peak window).

For transparency: we'll run two calculations for you tomorrow — (A) strict SLA-pro RATA using the standard formula, (B) a goodwill proposal that blends proration with a one-off uplift.

David Kim
Director, Account Management, Redwood Inference

-----

On Thu, 11 Apr 2029 at 08:35 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: alyssa.murray@quantapay.com
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: 2029-03-28 availability gap — confirmation & compensation

Alyssa — sorry again. Two quick notes on approach: 
1) For deals on a committed reserved plan (DP-48971), we typically calculate credit = (affected_time_minutes / total_minutes_in_billing_period) * monthly_commit_amount.
2) Where there is measurable business impact during peak windows, we have precedent to add a 10-20% goodwill uplift to expedite reconciliation.

I'll let Ops and Support present the timeline and traces; Marissa, can you package the raw traces + the service chronology CSV so we can produce the SLA_calc_sheet?

-Karthik

-----

Cc: alyssa.murray@quantapay.com

Subject: Re: 2029-03-28 availability gap — confirmation & compensation

Alyssa / team — attaching the raw telemetry snapshot and a short chronology we compiled from control-plane and edge traces.

Attachment summary: service-chronology.csv (minute-level events), trace_bundle.tar.gz (raw spans and aggregator logs).

Prelim timeline (conservative):
- 03:38:12 UTC: first 503 observed by edge (partial routing failure)
- 03:44:50 UTC: autoscaler misapplied policy; host eviction overlaps prefix cache leading to higher tail latencies
- 04:12:33 UTC: routing fallback completes; errors taper
- 04:17:09 UTC: nominal service restored

I also included a small checksums file so you can match our traces to your client-side samples.

-Marissa
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: 2029-03-28 availability gap — confirmation & compensation

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for the samples and for joining the call earlier today. Good meeting. Below are the actionable items and our proposed next steps: 

1) Confirmed incident window (final): 2029-03-28T03:38:12Z -> 2029-03-28T04:17:09Z (US-WEST-2).
2) Evidence bundle delivered: trace_bundle.tar.gz, service-chronology.csv (attached).
3) SLA calculation: attached sla_calc_sheet.csv with both the strict pro-rata calculation and a goodwill uplift option.
   - Strict pro-rata credit: 0.9% of monthly committed spend (calculated by minutes impacted / minutes in billing month).
   - Goodwill proposal: 1.5% of monthly committed spend (includes 10% uplift).
4) Postmortem session: proposed agenda attached (postmortem-agenda.docx). We recommend a 45-minute session; available slots next week: Apr 15 (10:00 AM PT) or Apr 16 (02:00 PM PT).

Attachments: sla_calc_sheet.csv, postmortem-agenda.docx (both included in the Drive link below and attached for convenience).

If the numbers look reasonable, we'll raise the credit in billing (DP-48971) upon your confirmation and follow up with the postmortem deck the day after the session.

Apologies again — we appreciate your patience and partnership.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
